I spent the last five years building the design infrastructure that lets large product organizations move fast without losing cohesion, which is exactly the challenge of owning a member experience across mobile and web.

At Zalando, I built and maintained the design system used by 40 product teams, cutting component duplication by 62% through consolidating the Figma library. That kind of systems thinking is what makes a persistent, personalized surface like CB1 Member Home hold together across every entry point instead of fragmenting over time. Earlier, at SoundCloud, I led a brand refresh spanning web and mobile and redesigned the mobile upload flow, lifting completion 24%, so I know what it takes to ship consumer-facing products end to end and see the impact land in real usage numbers.

I also ran accessibility audits that brought checkout to WCAG AA compliance at Zalando, which speaks to the same care for craft and consistency that a subscriber-facing product at this scale demands.

I'd welcome a short call to talk through how this experience maps to the CB1 Member Home work.

At Zalando, I built and maintained the design system used by 40 product teams, cutting component duplication 62% by consolidating the Figma library. I'm drawn to this role because Order Quality sits at exactly that intersection: high-visibility, cross-platform, and dependent on a design system that scales across teams. That's the kind of problem I've been solving, just at a different company.

That work only matters if it holds up under real product pressure, which is why I also ran the accessibility audits that brought checkout to WCAG AA compliance. Before that, at SoundCloud, I redesigned the mobile upload flow end to end and lifted completion 24%, then led the brand refresh across web and mobile. Both experiences taught me that consumer-facing products live or die on the details between concept and delivery, not just the concept itself.

I'm drawn to this role because Order Quality sits at exactly that intersection: high-visibility, cross-platform, and dependent on a design system that scales across teams. That's the kind of problem I've been solving, just at a different company.

I'd welcome a short call to talk through how my background in design systems and end-to-end consumer product work could apply to Order Quality at Instacart.
